subject: FathomAI renewal: reserved pool boost and throughput addendum
messages:
From: Clara Chen <clara@fathom.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@fathom.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning + request to double reserved GPUs (16→32)

Hi Sofia,

Hope you’re well — our renewal is coming up in June and we want to include an upgrade in the new commitment. Over the last 6 months we’ve run near cap on our 16 reserved GPUs during peak daytime inference and expect sustained growth from a new streaming feature.

Ask: can Redwood support a 16→32 reserved GPU migration at renewal with a throughput SLO (daily tokens) and a revised per-hour reserved price? Procurement is treating this as a single-line item so we need a clear per-GPU per-hour rate, a short ramp plan, and a simple addendum we can attach to the PO.

Attached is our internal demand rollup for the next 12 months — it shows ramping load and expected percent of burst usage. We’re targeting a 12-month term with a staged activation (8 GPUs in month 1, 24 by month 2, full 32 by month 3). Can you share a commercial proposal and any throughput guardrails you’d recommend?

Thanks,
Clara Chen
Head of Platform, FathomAI
[Attachment: FathomAI_Demand_Rollup.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning + request to double reserved GPUs (16→32) — pricing/SLA inputs needed

Team — FYI, FathomAI wants to double their reserved pool at renewal and they want a per-hour reserved rate plus throughput SLO. See attached demand.

Key asks:
- Can we support 32 reserved GPUs for a 12-month commit with a staged ramp?
- Suggested per-GPU reserved hourly rate for a mid-market 12mo commit (they’re current growth account).
- Recommended throughput SLO (tokens/day) tied to guaranteed capacity and the wording for an addendum.

Thinking out loud: offer a tiered hourly floor with a small burst allowance (10% buffer for first 60 days). If we can guarantee warmed KV-cache pools and pre-warmed batched slices, that helps latency during peak.

Ping me numbers — I’ll send a first-pass offer to Clara tomorrow.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + request to double reserved GPUs — pricing sketch

Sofia — quick sketch below (cost + operational constraints):

Operational notes:
- We can schedule a staged activation across 3 weeks to match their ramp plan; will require capacity carve-out in the pool and KV warm-up window.
- Recommend a 10% burst buffer for month 1–2, then 5% ongoing as part of our standard burst policy.

Commercial sketch (per-GPU reserved rates):
- Option A (12mo straight commit): $3.85 / GPU-hour baseline for the full 32 (blended).
- Option B (12mo with 2mo ramp credit): $3.45 / GPU-hour baseline + 8% credit applied to first 2 months of usage.
- Option C (higher SLA + throughput guarantee): $4.10 / GPU-hour but includes explicit throughput SLO and increased support hours.

Throughput SLO suggestion: guarantee 110–130M tokens/day (based on their forecast) for the 32 pool. Measure with token billing and a 15-minute rolling window SLA on 95th percentile latency tail; exceptions trigger credits (standard formula).

If you want to be aggressive on price for expansion, push Option B as our anchor — gives room to concede some list price without compromising committed revenue.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Chen <clara@fathom.ai>
Cc: procurement@fathom.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: 32-reserved GPU plan + throughput addendum (initial offer)

Clara — thanks for the demand file. Based on your ramp and usage profile, Redwood can support the 16→32 reserved GPU migration at renewal. Below is our initial commercial proposal you can attach to the PO.

Summary offer (initial):
- Capacity: 32 reserved GPUs (staged activation: 8 / 24 / 32 over first 3 months; exact schedule per your release plan)
- Term: 12 months starting on effective PO date
- Reserved per-hour rate (baseline): $3.85 per GPU-hour (blended)
- Burst buffer: 10% for months 1–2, then 5% ongoing
- Throughput SLO: 120M tokens/day guaranteed across the 32 pool (measured daily) with standard credit formula for missed SLA
- Ramp credit option: 8% credit applied to invoices covering months 1–2 if you elect the staged activation

Attached: SLA-Throughput-Addendum-v3.pdf with definitions and monitoring hooks. If you want a lower baseline rate we can move to the ramp-credit structure (Aditya/Ben recommended $3.45 effective with 8% ramp applied).

Next steps:
1) Confirm which pricing option you prefer (baseline $3.85 vs ramp-credit $3.45 effective).
2) Procurement to issue PO referencing the attached addendum.
3) We generate a DocuSign for the addendum and schedule the activation window.

Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the addendum.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA-Throughput-Addendum-v3.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Clara Chen <clara@fathom.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@fathom.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: 32-reserved GPU plan + throughput addendum (initial offer)

Hi Sofia — appreciate the quick turn. Procurement reviewed and they’re pushing back on the $3.85 baseline. Their target for budget planning is closer to $3.25 / GPU-hour with a 12-month term. They are willing to accept the staged ramp but want stronger language around credits if throughput drops below 95M tokens/day during the ramp. They also asked whether you can provide a 30-day pilot window at a lower pilot rate to validate the warmed pool behavior.

Can you do: 
- baseline target: $3.25 / GPU-hour (or blended equivalent with ramp credits),
- 30-day pilot at $2.50 / GPU-hour for up to 8 GPUs to validate,
- explicit credit formula for ramp months tied to 95M tokens/day floor.

Procurement needs a single-line item in the PO with the per-hour rate they approve to sign. If we can get a DocuSign ready with your preferred compromise, we can route internally quickly.

Thanks — Clara

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Chen <clara@fathom.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@fathom.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: 32-reserved GPU plan + throughput addendum (final counteroffer)

Clara — thanks for the clear ask and for looping procurement. We can meet you partway. Final commercial counteroffer below — crafted to keep your budget cadence intact while covering the operational cost of provisioning 32 reserved GPUs and the layered SLA you requested.

Final offer (counter):
- Capacity: 32 reserved GPUs; staged activation as requested (8 → 24 → 32 over 90 days max)
- Term: 12 months from PO effective date
- Reserved per-hour baseline: $3.45 / GPU-hour (blended)
- Ramp incentive: 8% credit applied to months 1–2 invoices (visible as line-item credit)
- Pilot: 30-day pilot for up to 8 GPUs at $2.75 / GPU-hour (we can run the pilot concurrently with contract signature; pilot billed separately and credit is non-recurring)
- Throughput SLO: 100M tokens/day floor during ramp months (month 1–2) with the following credit structure: if daily throughput < 100M tokens, credit = (shortfall_percent * daily_reserved_spend * 0.5) applied to invoice (language in attached addendum). Post-ramp SLO guaranteed at 120M tokens/day at 95th latency window as per addendum.

We will prepare a single-line PO attachment that lists the effective per-hour baseline ($3.45) and references the attached SLA-Throughput-Addendum (v3) for credit mechanics. I’ve generated a DocuSign envelope for the addendum and PO attachment so procurement can sign quickly: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/example/0a1b2c3d4e

If that pricing pushes you over budget, the remaining lever is decreasing the guaranteed post-ramp throughput or extending term — happy to discuss. If you’re good, please sign the DocuSign and we’ll schedule the activation and hold the reserved capacity.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | Account team: Ben Carter (Head of Sales), Aditya Rao (Solutions), Marissa Cole (Renewals)
[Attachment: SLA-Throughput-Addendum-v3.pdf (application/pdf)]
